en: The Scripture on Returning to Folly through Observing Transformations in the Śākya Clan:
Long ago, in the kingdom of Śrāvastī, there was a poor household whose husband and wife were stingy, wicked, and did not believe in the Way or its virtue.
Out of pity for their folly, the Buddha manifested as a śramaṇa and went to their door to beg for alms. At that time, the husband was not at home. His...
The woman reviled him without any reason.
The śramaṇa said to her,
"I am a man of the Way."
He sustains himself by begging;
he does not utter insults or abuse,
seeking only a single meal.
The hostess said, "If you were to die right now, you would still not even obtain food;
how much less so now that you are healthy and strong, do you expect my food?"
"However, it is better to depart early than to linger for so long.
Thereupon, the śramaṇa stood before him;
with a piercing gaze and a heavy sigh, he manifested himself as standing dead.
The body swelled, and worms emerged from its nose and mouth;
the abdomen burst open and the intestines rotted away, with impurities flowing out in profusion.
When his wife saw this, she was struck with terror, let out a cry, and fled, abandoning him.
Thereupon, the practitioner suddenly departed.
Having traveled several li, he sat beneath a tree to rest.
As her husband returned home, he encountered his wife on the road.
Wondering at his alarm and fear,
his wife said to her husband,
"There is a śramaṇa who has frightened you so much."
The husband asked with great anger, "Where has she gone?
The wife replied, "She has already left;
I think she has not gone far."
Thereupon, grasping his bow and girding on his sword, he followed the tracks to pursue him;
drawing his bow and unsheathing his blade,
he ran forward, intending to strike the practitioner.
The practitioner of the Way immediately manifested a city of lapis lazuli to surround himself.
The man circled the city several times but was unable to enter.
He asked the practitioner, "Why have you not opened the door?
The practitioner replied,
"I wish for the door to open so that I may cast away your bow and sword."
The man thought to himself, "I must follow his words;
if I can get my hands on him, I shall strike him with my fist.
Thereupon, he immediately cast away his bow and sword.
The gate did not open.
He said to the practitioner,
"I have already cast away my bow and sword."
"Why is the gate not open?
The practitioner said,
"I have caused you to discard the bow and sword of evil intent within your mind."
"It does not mean the bow and sword in my hand.
Thereupon, his heart was startled and his body trembled;
he realized that the practitioner was divine and holy, and thus knew his thoughts.
Even as he knelt with his head to the ground in repentance,
he addressed the practitioner, saying:
"I have a wretched wife who does not recognize a true person."
"May you share this enmity with me;
I pray that you will deign to show us some compassion and not abandon us.
We now wish to bring them here to exhort them to cultivate the Path."
He immediately rose and returned home.
His wife asked him,
"Where is the śramaṇa?"
Her husband recounted the deity’s virtues in detail:
"The deity is currently in that village;
you should go there yourself to repent and extinguish your transgressions."
Thereupon, the husband and wife went to the place where the practitioner was;
prostrating themselves with their five limbs to repent for their transgressions, they vowed to become his disciples.
Kneeling upright, they asked:
The spiritual transformations and sacred attainments of this practitioner are such as these.
There is a city of lapis lazuli, firm and difficult to surpass;
his resolve is clear and his mind is settled, forever free from sorrow and affliction.
"What path of virtue and what moral conduct have you practiced to attain such spiritual wonder?
The practitioner replied,
"I have studied extensively without weariness, upholding the Dharma."
Through unremitting diligence, maintaining the precepts, wisdom, and heedfulness,
one attains the Way by means of these conditions and personally reaches Nirvana.
Thereupon, the practitioner spoke these verses:
"Much learning, when held with firmness, And the Dharma practiced as a protective wall, Are difficult for diligence to surpass;
from this, precepts and wisdom are perfected. Much learning makes the mind clear; With clarity, wisdom increases."
Wisdom brings broad understanding of meaning; seeing the meaning, one dwells in peace through practicing the Dharma. Great learning can remove sorrow, and through concentration, one finds joy.
Skillfully expounding the nectar-like Dharma, one knows for oneself the attainment of Nirvana.
Through hearing, one comes to know the Dharma and Vinaya; resolving doubts, one also sees the truth. By means of hearing, one abandons what is not the Dharma.
When they had reached the Immortal Abode and the practitioner had finished reciting the verse, he manifested the radiant marks of a Buddha;
its vast brilliance blazed forth, illuminating heaven and earth.
The husband and wife were struck with awe, their spirits trembling with fear.
Reforming his resentment and cleansing his heart, he struck his head against the ground;
having destroyed twenty billion evils, he attained the stage of Srotāpanna.
